argument: Within autonomous driving pipeline, decomposing the driving task into DNN-based waypoint prediction plus an algorithmic controller for steering and throttle is associated with reduced need for human-generated training data and increased flexibility across different vehicles, including vehicle replacement or tuning without network retraining under advantageous compared with end-to-end learned vehicle control.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported simulator-based driving case study and its experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
claim: Decomposing autonomous driving into a learned waypoint-prediction module and an algorithmic vehicle-control module, instead of learning vehicle controls end-to-end, reduces reliance on human driving data and increases flexibility across different vehicles, allowing vehicle replacement or tuning without retraining the network.
conditions: the perception module predicts waypoints ahead of the car
the control module is a separate algorithmic controller
training data are auto-generated waypoints rather than human driving demonstrations
falsifier: On a fixed driving task, compare an end-to-end control-learning pipeline with a waypoint-prediction-plus-algorithmic-control pipeline, measuring human-data requirements, retraining needs after vehicle changes, and success on lane-change and obstacle-avoidance maneuvers.
interpretation: The evidence supports a design rule or intervention concerning autonomous driving pipeline.
